summary: Retested the CDR upload 500 ('Mixed timezones detected'). The 500 is fixed: none of the timestamp styles tested return 500 any more, through the API or the UI. The parser fix is still incomplete, though. A CDR where every timestamp has a non-UTC zone name (e.g. all 'EST') is rejected with 400 'No rows had a readable date/time'. EST values mixed with naive times are silently dropped as invalid. UTC names, mixed ISO offsets (-05:00/+00:00/Z) with naive times, +0000/-0500, US AM/PM, epoch s/ms, blank rows and EST+UTC mixes all import with correct UTC. CLI matching (both upload orders), cli_matched in the response, and the reset of matched CLIs on CDR delete all work. Backend: 11 of 13 pytest pass. UI: the Uploads -> CDR report -> mapping-step -> import flow works; the EST-only file shows the 400 toast.

critical.issue: Timestamps with tz abbreviations other than UTC/GMT (EST, EDT, CST, PST, IST, also lowercase 'utc') are turned into NaT silently. pandas 3.1.1 to_datetime(format='mixed', errors='coerce') coerces them without raising, so the dateutil fallback only runs when pandas happens to raise (e.g. EST mixed with UTC or offsets). Effects: a CDR with only 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS EST' rows -> 400 'No rows had a readable date/time'. 'EST' rows mixed with naive rows -> the EST rows are counted invalid. Fix: after the fast path, re-parse every non-blank value that came out NaT with _parse_one (or use the per-value path whenever raw contains [A-Za-z]{2,5}$). Also make the TZ_ABBR lookup case-insensitive.

minor.issue: A file mixing epoch values with date strings: the epoch rows become NaT because the epoch branch needs all values to be epoch.

Naive times in the DST fall-back hour (e.g. 2026-11-01 01:30 America/New_York) become NaT (ambiguous='NaT') and are counted invalid. The fallback path keeps them (fold=0), so the two paths behave differently. Consider ambiguous='infer' or fold=0 to match.
dd/mm/yyyy dates are read as mm/dd (e.g. '01/11/2026' -> Jan 11). This is expected for US Primo exports; just noting it.

action_items: Fix parse_ts so values with tz abbreviations that pandas coerces to NaT are re-parsed with _parse_one (EST-only files currently fail with 400, and EST rows mixed with naive rows are dropped).
Optional: case-insensitive tz abbreviations; handle epoch values mixed with date strings; handle DST-ambiguous naive times the same way in both paths.

rca of the issue: Original 500: pandas raised 'Mixed timezones detected' inside parse_ts. It now hits the dateutil fallback, or returns 400 via the new try/except. Remaining bug: pandas 3.x to_datetime(format='mixed', errors='coerce') returns NaT for strings ending in zone names it doesn't know (EST etc.) and does not raise, so the fallback is skipped. Reproduce: commit a kind=cdr CSV with 'Start Time' = '2026-11-20 10:00:00 EST' -> 400 No rows had a readable date/time. Mitigation: per-value fallback for every non-blank NaT.
